input.brief: Jaswant Singh, New Delhi web and AI developer. Connected systems from travel bookings to WordPress AI to Shopify commerce. Charcoal opening, off-white asymmetric project chapters, cobalt accents, Inter type, architectural 3D.

direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Window that opens to the edges
hero.blueprint: A flat paper or pale ground, and one picture seen through a small window that becomes the whole screen as the page scrolls. The hero is a wrapper 200svh tall holding a stage with `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`. On the first frame the window is a 4:5 portrait opening 36% of the viewport wide (518×648px), centred, its top and bottom 126px from the edges, square corners; give it a shape from the subject if it has one (an arch, a rounded diamond, a lens). Build it as `clip-path: inset(126px 461px)` on a layer that is itself 100vw by 100svh, so the photograph or muted film inside is laid out full-bleed and never moves: only the opening grows. The headline sits left of the window on columns 1–3: two lines at clamp(44px, 4.4vw, 64px), leading 0.95, flush to the 32px margin, its last baseline level with the window's lower edge. Right of the window on columns 10–12, bottom-aligned to the same line: one supporting sentence at 18px, max 26ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Wordmark top-left and three text links top-right at 15px on the same margin; nothing else sits on the ground. Over the first 100svh of scroll the inset runs to zero on a scroll-linked timeline while the text, which sits above the picture layer, rises and fades out before the opening reaches it; the picture then holds full-bleed for 50svh before the next section slides over it. Without scroll timelines, or under reduced motion, show the open picture with the headline over a neutral scrim in its bottom-left corner.
hero.mobile: The stage stays sticky. The window starts 78vw wide at 4:5, centred, its top at 30% of the height, leaving about a quarter of the screen below it. The headline sits above it at 10vw on two lines inside 20px margins, 72px down; the supporting sentence at 16px and a full-width action sit under the window. The opening reaches the edges within 70svh of scroll. The links fold behind a menu word.
hero.headline: Two short lines of up to about 9 characters each: the name with what it is, or a 2–4 word claim. It scrolls away as the picture takes the screen.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One frame, three distances
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. On the stage one frame is centred: 30vw wide at 4:5, square corners, overflow hidden. Inside it the same photograph is shown at three distances as the reader scrolls: the whole subject, then scaled to 180% toward one detail, then to 320% on a second detail (transform: scale with a transform-origin per stage, 700ms ease, switched by IntersectionObserver on three invisible markers). The sentence is delivered in halves: its first two or three words sit above the frame at clamp(56px, 8vw, 130px), centred; the last words arrive below the frame at the second stage, overlapping the frame's bottom edge by 0.3em. At the third stage one caption of 28ch at 17px appears to the right of the frame, top-aligned. The two halves together are the heading and stay within two lines.
sections.mobile: The frame grows to 70vw at 4:5 and stays sticky at centre. The first half of the sentence sits above it at 13vw, the second half below it at the same size. The third-stage caption appears under the sentence at 16px, centred.

sections.name: One scene, stepping statements
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 350–450vh tall holds a sticky full-bleed photograph (100vw by 100svh) with a calm, symmetrical subject and a clear upper third; a neutral dark scrim covers only that upper third. At top centre, five or six short statements of two to five words are stacked at 18–20px with 10px between them; the first of them is the section's heading. One statement is at full white and the rest at 45% opacity; the active line steps down the stack as the reader scrolls (IntersectionObserver on invisible 70vh markers). For each statement, two small photographs with square corners, 160–240px wide and of different ratios, fade in left and right of the centre line at different heights, then leave when the next pair arrives. No other text. A low-key image on a deep ground works equally well.
sections.mobile: The photograph stays sticky at 100svh, cropped to its centre. The statement stack moves to the bottom third over a scrim, at 17px, left-aligned on the margin. Each statement brings one small photograph only, 44vw wide, placed in the top-right corner with a 16px margin.

sections.name: Pinned title, portraits pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people. A `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds the heading, two words at clamp(88px, 12vw, 180px), leading 0.85, centred at mid-height, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads over ground and photographs alike. Beneath it in the stacking order, portraits scroll past in normal flow: each a 4:5 photograph 26–30vw wide, alternately starting at column 2 and ending at column 11, 60svh apart, so each one passes behind a different half of the heading. Under each portrait's left corner: the name at 18px, the role at 14px in the soft ink, and one sentence of up to 30 words in a 280px measure. The last portrait is followed by 40svh of empty ground before the heading releases. Square corners. Nothing else is on screen.
sections.mobile: The heading shrinks to 17vw and pins 16px from the top instead of at mid-height. Portraits become 72% wide, alternating between the left and right margins, 48px apart, each with name, role and sentence beneath at the portrait's width.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

references.name: NORMAL IS BORING
references.idea: The brand name is split and half of it turned upside down: a plain sans first word top-left and a serif last word flipped 180 degrees bottom-right stay fixed while panels slide sideways between them.
references.hero: A white panel fills the left 80%; a full-height interior photo takes the right 20%. Top-left: the first word of the name in light geometric capitals, about 56px. Bottom-right of the white panel: an italic 'is' above the last word in bold didone, rotated 180 degrees so it reads upside down. Three small caps nav links run vertically up the panel's right edge. The 50px headline is broken into three two-line fragments on different columns and baselines: one at 21% from the left, one a line lower at 42%, one back at 21% whose last word turns bold italic didone. A seven-line 13px paragraph hangs beneath the middle fragment.
references.type: Izmir, a light geometric sans in capitals, for wordmark, hero fragments and 13px body; Juana, a high-contrast didone, bold italic for accent words and huge roman capitals (10-12vw and larger, cropped) for scrolling statements; Editorial New ultralight for the reversed paragraph.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #ece4da #c7d7e9 #db5c59 #1f9aa0 — White and black panels alternate with warm beige; pale blue and coral panels appear deeper in. Type stays black or white. A single teal dot acts as cursor; photos bring wood and plant tones.
references.imagery: Warm interior and garden photography of finished homes in natural light, wood and linen tones. Square-cornered; used as full-height strips, full-bleed panels and smaller insets laid over larger photos by about a third.
references.layout: Reads as a sideways journey: white, black and beige panels slide horizontally with photos and oversized words cropped by panel edges. Text fragments sit on an irregular grid; the two halves of the logo stay fixed in opposite corners.

sections.description: The photo strip from the hero grows to a full-height panel while a second, smaller interior photo slides over it, overlapping by roughly a third. To the right a white panel carries a four-line statement in didone capitals about 90px tall, set so the lines run off the panel edge and are completed only as scrolling continues. A small 12px paragraph sits under the statement's left edge.

Full black panel. A nine-line paragraph in an ultralight serif at about 32px starts 70% of the way across and runs off the right edge; its words fade from white through grey to near-black line by line as a scroll-driven reveal. A single photo of a pool at dusk, roughly 300px square, sits alone in the lower-left third. The menu pill and flipped logo invert to white.

Values panel on beige. Along the left edge a vertical ticker repeats one word in 90px didone capitals rotated 90 degrees, separated by thin eight-point asterisks. Beside it a large exterior photograph of a stone-and-glass house with a bathroom photo about half its size laid over its lower-right corner, square edges, no shadow or border.

Beige panel where the project title is set so large that single didone letters exceed the viewport height and are cropped top and bottom, acting as black shapes in the left half. In the right half a modest 300px-wide aerial photo floats with a bracketed year above and a centred serif caption and two-line descriptor below.

steal: Split a two-part brand name into opposite corners of the viewport and flip one half 180 degrees so the logo enacts the name.
Break a headline into fragments on different columns and baselines, like a stair, and hang the body paragraph under one fragment only.
Scale a project title until single letters are taller than the viewport, then float a small captioned photo beside those cropped shapes.
references.media: The only picture on the first screen is an interior photograph cropped to the right 20% (290px, full height), the leading edge of a pinned horizontal track that widens to about 65% on the next screen. Inside the track, overlapping pairs lay a smaller photograph over a larger full-height one, project cards widen as they reach the centre, and a photograph sits framed in a flat coral field; all 29 images have square corners and reveal by clip-path while scaling down from 1.5, and there is no video.
references.motion: About 2.5s of entrance: the logo, then headline characters, then body lines rising from masks (y over 0.65-0.97s power3.out at a 0.025-0.033 stagger), then the photo and nav. One section pins for +=1150% (about 10,350px) at scrub 1 and is translated sideways; photo pairs move on scrub 0.35, a statement fills line by line on scrub 0, and project cards widen over 1s power1.inOut; a dot cursor grows with a back-out overshoot the house layer does not use.

references.name: Glitch&Grit
references.idea: Every screen is one project: two half-width footage columns with the project name stacked dead centre across their seam in a single flat pastel that changes per project.
references.hero: Black viewport split down its vertical centre. The left half holds a huge flat grey flower silhouette bleeding off the left and bottom edges; the right half is black with a few tiny video thumbnails drifting through. Dead centre, straddling the split, sits a two-line uppercase title in mint green, about 11vw per line, lines almost touching, spanning roughly 70% of the width. Two tiny category lines sit directly above it and a tiny 'view full project' link directly below, all in the same green. Navigation is six small bold white words pinned to the frame: three links across the top edge, the three-part studio name across the bottom edge.
references.type: Elza only, weight 900, uppercase, tracking -0.05em so letters nearly collide, line-height under 1. Just two sizes exist: roughly 158px project titles and 12px bold caps for nav, tags and links, a 13:1 jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #000000 #999999 #9ae187 #93f1f7 #dcc8ff #fbb060 — Black ground and dark-graded footage. The only flat colour is the title lock-up, which takes a new candy pastel per project: mint, cyan, lilac, cornflower, lemon, orange.
references.imagery: Client film footage in two half-width columns per screen, cropped tight, graded dark, square edges, the two columns vertically offset against each other. One flat grey cut-out flower shape opens the sequence.
references.layout: No margins or containers. Each project is a full viewport cut into two equal media columns with one centred title lock-up. Fixed corner navigation frames every screen; fourteen screens repeat the same slide with different footage and title colour.

sections.description: Each scroll stop is a project slide. Two half-width media columns fill the viewport edge to edge and travel vertically at different offsets, so their top and bottom seams never align. Centred over the join: a two-line 11vw uppercase title in one flat pastel, with two or three 12px tag lines stacked above and a 12px 'view full project' or 'coming soon' line beneath. Title colour changes on every slide; nothing else does.

There is no footer block. The last screen is simply another project slide, and the studio name fixed along the bottom edge in three pieces (first word bottom-left, ampersand bottom-centre, last word bottom-right) does the footer's job on every screen, mirroring the three nav words fixed along the top edge at the same size and weight.

steal: Break the studio name into three words pinned bottom-left, bottom-centre and bottom-right, mirroring three nav links across the top, so the viewport frame itself is the logo.
Give each project slide one flat pastel used only for its title and tags, so a colour change is the sole signal that the project changed.
Split the viewport into two media columns that scroll at different offsets and set the title across the seam so the type stitches the halves together.
references.media: Media fills the whole first screen: a flat grey cut-out flower on the left half and a scatter of small thumbnails on the right that grows into a collage round the title. Then video is the main medium: each project is two full 720x900 half panes of muted, looping footage moving in opposite directions, with the title straddling the seam; about 24 pieces of footage or illustration across twelve projects.
references.motion: After a 10.7s load the thumbnail grid fills the right half by 1.2s and scales into a cluster by 4.5s, and Lenis then runs 40 scrubbed ScrollTriggers on empty 855px track divs: per project the left pane and half-title travel one way and the right ones the other (titles ±270px, panes ±180px), lining up only at the centre, and the scroll resets for an endless loop. Panes grow from an edge by scaleY over 0.5s, tags slide on y over 0.5s power2, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.
